title: They laughed at the story…
paragraphs:
They laughed at the story…
not realizing the story was about them.
Because this is where most people miss it.
Jesus didn’t speak in parables because the truth was complicated.
He spoke in parables because the human heart is.

A farmer throwing seeds.
A son running away.
A shepherd chasing one lost sheep.

Because while the story sounds ordinary…
it’s cutting through your defenses.
When Jesus Christ spoke, crowds gathered. Thousands. Curious. Hungry. Skeptical.
But not all of them left changed.
In Matthew 13, the disciples asked what you’ve probably wondered:
“Why do You speak to them in parables?”
And Jesus answered with a truth that should shake us:
“Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.” (Matthew 13:13)
They reveal what’s already inside you.

To the humble…
they unlock revelation.

To the proud…
they sound like riddles.
And here’s the part most people won’t say out loud:
Jesus wasn’t trying to make everyone comfortable.

And just like that…
the crowd separated itself.
That’s not just a beautiful story.

That’s your rebellion.
Your running.
Your hunger.
That’s God—waiting, watching, ready to embrace the moment you turn.

That’s about you wandering…
and a Savior who refuses to leave you there.
They receive it fast—but walk away when life gets hard.
“What kind of heart do you have?”

Because you can hear truth every day…
and still never be changed.
And this is why Jesus spoke the way He did.
Not to hide truth from the sincere…
But don’t miss the mercy in this.
Because every parable is also an invitation.
To stop hiding behind religion, image, or intellect.
You are not just the listener in the story.
You are the sinner in need of saving.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
But here’s where the story flips.
Because Jesus didn’t just tell parables.
He became the Good Shepherd who lays down His life.
He became the Seed that dies to bring life.
He became the Son who was rejected… so we could be accepted.
At the cross, the story reached its climax.
And now the invitation is open.
Not just to understand a story…
…but to be transformed by the Savior behind it.
Don’t treat this like just another post.
What is your heart like today?
Because the same words you just read…
If you feel something stirring right now…
Jesus is not hiding from you.
the parables will stop being confusing—
And don’t keep the truth locked inside a story.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
